Subject: Performance qualification: Private VPC — latency, throughput, concurrency (next steps)

Hi Elena / Finexa infra team,

Thanks again for the hour today — good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the Private VPC performance qualification so we can lock acceptance criteria and schedule a smoke window.

Recap of targets we heard on the call (please correct if I misunderstood):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end token latency target <= 120ms for 256-token responses (streaming enabled).
- Throughput: sustained aggregate target ~1,200 tokens/sec across the deployment; ability to absorb 10k tokens/sec burst for up to 2 minutes.
- Concurrency: support 250 parallel active sessions with per-session sequential streaming (server push / HTTP/2).
- Streaming requirements: gRPC/HTTP2 streaming preferred; we also support chunked HTTP/1.1 fallback.
- Egress constraints: Finexa noted outbound egress caps on some subnets — need exact numbers and static IP ranges to validate.

What we need from you to proceed with the lab run:
1) Confirm the p95 target above and tell us which endpoints will originate traffic (VPC CIDR / static egress IP ranges).
2) Provide any per-subnet egress limits (Mbps) or NAT gateway capacity constraints.
3) Confirm whether traffic will route over a peered VPC (AWS peering), site-to-site VPN, or ExpressRoute — and the expected hop count/typical RTT to our peering location.
4) Allowlist the redwood test IPs (we'll send these) and open TCP ports 443 and 50051 for the test window.
5) If you require mTLS, tell us the CA bundle and SNI details for mutual auth.

Attached: redwood-acceptance-matrix.csv (proposed pass/fail criteria) and test-instructions.md (how we run the smoke tests and what telemetry we'll collect).

Proposed timeline:
- You provide items 1–4 by EOD 2028-06-14.
- Redwood SRE runs a preflight probe on 2028-06-16 (non-invasive).
- Full streaming + burst test window: 2028-06-19 02:00–04:00 UTC.

If any of those dates don't work, call out alternatives. We'll scope the lab to avoid production impact — tests can be run against a sandbox VPC or behind a temporary ingress rule.

Thanks,

--
Stephanie Nguyen

Thanks Stephanie — nice summary. A few clarifications and the infra details you requested below.

Confirmations / notes:
- The p95 <= 120ms is reasonable as a target for short-response flows; we'll validate against our long-tail jobs separately.
- Our traffic will originate from a set of NATs in our eu-west-1 VPCs. We can provide the exact egress IP ranges and the subnets by tomorrow.
- Egress: currently we have soft caps of 150 Mbps per NAT gateway in the primary VPC. We have one standby NAT in another AZ.
- Connectivity: we prefer to peer VPCs (AWS VPC peering) to avoid VPN churn; however, for compliance some workloads must go over our site-to-site VPN. We'll confirm which path for the test. Expect 2–3 hops and typical RTT to your peering edge ~18–24 ms.
- Ports: 443 is fine; can also open 50051 for gRPC if needed.
- mTLS: we can support mTLS, but we'll need a CSR/CAs for mutual auth; send instructions if you need us to install certs before the window.

Action items from Finexa (I'll own these):
- Share egress IP ranges and subnet names by 2028-06-14 EOD.
- Confirm whether the test uses peering or VPN by 2028-06-15.
- Provide support contact for SRE on test day (we'll give a mobile number).

One question from our infra lead: what kind of burst shaping do you apply on the Redwood side? Specifically, do you buffer and throttle at the connection edge or is the model serving layer expected to handle token bursts?

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rossi

Forwarding a technical plan for the lab run — copied Elena for visibility.

Stephanie / Elena,

High-level test plan and internal notes:
- Burst handling: Redwood applies adaptive ingress shaping at the edge and transparent backpressure to the serving layer. For short bursts (<= 2 minutes) we allow token-level oversubscription up to 5x baseline across the cluster; we expect bursts to be absorbed by warm KV caches. If your egress cap is lower than the effective bandwidth needed, we'll see queueing at the NAT and higher request RTTS — hence the importance of knowing per-NAT Mbps.

- Streaming protocol: gRPC/HTTP2 streaming gives best p95 stability. We recommend using HTTP/2 with stream multiplexing for the test. Fallback to chunked HTTP/1.1 is available but increases p95 by ~30–60ms in our experience.

- Connection recommendations:
  * Keepalive: 30s (server) / 60s (client)
  * TLS session resumption enabled
  * MTU: default 1500 is fine; if you have jumbo frames (9001) please flag it — that can help throughput.
  * Idle timeout: 120s for test harness sessions.

- Warm-up: run 15 min warm-up per route to prime KV cache and compilation kernels.

- Test harness: we'll run the streaming-smoke-plan.txt (attached) which executes:
  1) Baseline steady-state: 1,200 tokens/sec for 10 minutes
  2) Burst ramp: 10k tokens/sec for up to 2 minutes, repeated 3x with 5m recovery
  3) Concurrency stress: ramp to 250 parallel streams with small (8–64 token) responses to exercise connection churn

- Telemetry we will collect (and ask you to collect):
  * Client-side: per-connection RTT, packet loss (from tcpdump if available), per-stream latency distribution
  * Network: traceroute/mtr to our peering IPs, and tcpdump during the window (packet-capture-guidance.txt attached)
  * Redwood: per-model p50/p95/p99, token throughput, node cpu/gpu utilization, queue depth over time

Proposed small dev tasks for our side before the window:
- Send redwood test egress IPs (we will do this by EOD).
- Generate CSR for mTLS if Finexa will enable mutual auth (Karthik will prepare instructions).

Scheduling: 2028-06-19 02:00–04:00 UTC looks OK for our SREs. We'll staff a runbook channel and a rollback plan (immediate cut to single-model fallback) in case we hit infra limits.

Attachments: streaming-smoke-plan.txt, packet-capture-guidance.txt

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
